Second, they brought not only fresh capital (huge inflows) but new management, 3 See: - finance/foc_conf_website_marko_skreb_website.pdf modern techniques, and in general best (or at least better than earlier) practices. They increased competition, so domestically owned banks had to adapt and become better. The key word here is increased competition and benefits for consumers. I hope I have successfully demonstrated why EU should remain goal for this part of the world. I ask doubting Thomases, what are the alternatives to this path? Where do we go from here? As the world is changing countries must continue to reform whether to Converge or correct macroeconomic imbalances or not. Panta rhei as Heraclitus said. Everything is flowing. So are our economies. To end my speech let me share with you four lessors I consider relevant on this topic4. Lesson 1: Rome was not built in a day. We, people from Southeast Europe are impatient. We expected higher living standards (like Germany at least) and developed institutions in a short period of time. When thinking about future progress we need to be patient. Therefore, looking backwards and acknowledging the tremendous progress we have achieved is not only beneficial as motivation for the future, but also necessary to keep reform mojo alive. Lesson 2: We must indeed all hang together, or most assuredly, we shall hang separately. It seems that the UK has forgotten this old Benjamin Franklins admonition. Pity, as the whole Brexit process is proof of how painful a divorce from the EU can be. I am convinced that despite drawbacks, being part of EU and hang together helps us especially in hard times. Lesson 3: Every action creates a reaction. This Newtonian Law applied to economic reforms works and should be remembered. Typically, every reform redistributes income. Thus, there are losers and winners of reforms. To minimize obstacles to reforms, it is imperative to think about the losers, compensate them in one way or another and try to create win-win situations. It seems that this was widely forgotten in the past, income and wealth inequalities have grown significantly5 and in the post- Picketty world populism is on the rise. 4 Partly based on: - people-isnt-it/ 5 I refer to inequalities within mostly advanced economies. Lesson 4: Keep Darwin alive. Competition policies are more important than ever. Even in a single EU market, a concentration of BigTech companies (Google, Amazon, Facebook and Apple, but others as well) are only one of many cases where additional regulation and competition policies must be preserved. Do you think that a small country like Croatia can better stand against Facebook or Google then Ms. Verstager the new-old EC commissioner and vice president can? The EU was, and still is, the main magnet for many countries in South East Europe and generator of needed reforms. So convergence must continue. Concluding remarks. In 1963 at the peak of the Cold War, JF Kennedy ended his famous speech with the following words: Ich bin Ein Berliner. He never dreamed that a quarter of a century later the wall would collapse. Allow me to paraphrase JFK and say: Ja sam Sarajlija. And I mean this not only metaphorically. When I did the math, it turned out I have spent almost full four years of my life in Sarajevo. I hope that this Conference, and in general work done by CBBH on a broader scale is the step toward joining the big EU family. Thank you all once again for this great Conference.

Title: To the German business community in
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: THE PART OF THE SPEECH OF GOVERNOR OF CENTRAL BANK OF BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA PETER NICHOLL TO THE GERMAN BUSINESS COMMUNITY IN SARAJEVO 13 SEPTEMBER 2001 In the Central Bank Law 1 KM 1 DEM. We will take the DEM exchange rate out of the CBBH Law shortly and substitute the Euro exchange rate, so 1 KM 0,51129 EURO. The Currency board arrangement will not change in any way except that the anchor currency will be the EURO, not the DM. The exchange rate will still be fixed, the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina will still need to provide at least 100% backing in convertible foreign currency for all our KM liabilities and the KM will be fully convertible, but to EURO rather than the DM. Bosnia and Herzegovina is possibly ahead of other Eastern European countries as we have been changing DEM cash to some other financial assets for three years already. We have an established process for transferring the foreign currency banknotes and we can continue to use it up until February 28,2002. Customers will continue to take their Eurozone banknotes to commercial banks and the banks in turn will send it to the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina and we will send it to the banks in Germany. We will reopen the window for people to exchange DM coins for a two week period at the end of November 2001. This will apply only to DM coins. At present people in BH have three choices with what they can convert Euro zone currencies to: a KM banknote, another foreign currency such as the Swiss frank or US dollar; a bank deposit, either here or abroad and either in KM or a foreign currency, including Euro. From 1 January 2002 they will have a four choice  to convert it in the commercial banks to Euro banknotes. We will try and ensure there are enough Euro banknotes here to allow people to do that if they wish. But people need to remember that DM, French Franc, Euro are foreign currencies and it is not an obligation to the CBBH to ensure people can change one to the other. Our obligation is to ensure that people can change foreign currencies to KM and convert them back again without limit. We will encourage citizens in Bosnia and Herzegovina to exchange their Eurozone currencies until the end of February 2002. Afterwards the costs would be probably higher and procedure of conversion, requested from the Eurozone national banks, will be longer. From 1st January 2002 the only legal tender currency in Bosnia and Herzegovina will continue to be KM. The Euro will not be legal tender but neither it will be an illegal currency. Therefore if someone offers to pay in Euro, the seller can choose whether or not to accept it  and what exchange rate they will accept it. The Euro will not be as convenient as a joint currency alongside the KM as the DM was because of the exchange rate. With a KM/DM exchange rate of 1:1, the two currencies could be and were used interchangeably. This is unlikely to happen with the Euro so that people will have to pay in one or the other rather than in a mixture. It will be interesting to see to what extent the Euro is used as a transactions currency in BH. The Euro wont be as convenient as joint currency alongside the KM as the DEM was because of exchange rate. With a KM/DEM exchange rate of 1/1, the two currencies could be and were used interchangeably. This is unlikely to happen with Euro so that people will have to pay in one or the other rather than in a mixture. It will be interesting to see to what extent the Euro is used as a transactions currency in BiH. The banking sector in BiH: Four years ago, there were around 76 organisations authorised to be banks in BiH. But none of them operated over the whole country, most of them were incredibly small, and they did little traditional banking i.e. Taking deposits and lending. It was a very strange banking system!!! There have been substantial improvements, particularly over the last year. The number of banks has reduced with 42 now taking part in the new payments system, there are 6 or 7 banks operating in both entities, some good foreign banks have come into the market, citizens are gradually starting to trust some of the banks, and deposit with them and some banks are beginning to lend. There is still a long way to go before BiH has a banking sector that can play the major economic role that the banking sector plays in most other countries in Europe, including in most other transition economies in Eastern Europe. But 2000 and 2001 will be seen as two years in which the banking sector in BiH finally began to move in the right direction and I believe that speed of change will continue to accelerate. I will briefly list the main changes that have brought this about: First, the payments system underwent fundamental reform. The old state-owned centralised system that had a monopoly was closed. It has been replaced with modern European-type system with two clearing houses, an RTGS one and a GIRO one, owned and operated by the Central Bank. Payments are being conducted by the commercial banks. The suppliers we used had put similar systems into place in nine other European countries. But it was done more quickly than anywhere else showing that it is possible to implement large, technical projects in BiH successfully. It has been operating since 5th January 2001 and is going very smoothly. We have done 7,5 million transactions worth 10,5 billion in our new internal payments system over the first eight months of operation. Second, minimum capital requirements for banks were substantially increased, forcing banks to merge or find strategic partners. Third, it became possible for a bank registered in one entity to operate branches in the other entity. Five banks are already doing so and more will follow. Fourth, more foreign banks commenced operations in BiH in 2000, either by applying for licenses directly or by purchasing an existing BiH bank. Increased foreign competition will be very good for the BiH economy. It will give depositors more choice and will force the local banks to improve range and quality of the services they provide if they want to survive. One can already see these effects occurring. Fifth, a limited deposit insurance scheme has started which should help return citizens confidence to the banks that qualify. So far, only four banks have been admitted to the scheme and it is only operating in the federation. Sixth, most of the state-owned banks (there are still nineteen state or mainly-state owned banks in BiH) finally have their opening balance sheets approved and they moved into the privatisation phase. But progress in bank privatisation continued to be very slow over the past year. While this is disappointing, in my view it is no longer critical for the process of bank reform in BiH as the reform process is being largely driven by private-owned banks, including the recently arrived foreign banks. The citizens actually show a higher degree of trust in privately-owned banks. While at first sight, this might seem to be paradoxical it is completely understandable once one knows a bit of the financial history of the region. For example, in the Federation of BiH, 65% of citizens deposits are in the banks covered by the deposit insurance scheme, 76% are in foreign-owned banks, and 93% are in privately-owned banks. What lies ahead in the banking sector for the rest of 2001 and 2002? The degree of foreign ownership will increase; The number of banks will decrease substantially under the combined pressure of higher capital requirements and sharply increased competition; A single deposit insurance agency will be established and more banks will be eligible for insurance; Banking supervision, currently carried out by entity agencies, will come under the umbrella of the CBBH; The range and quality of services will continue to improve; The degree of state involvement in the banking sector will decrease substantially through the privatisation or closure of state owned banks. In short, the BiH banking system will start to look more and more like the banking system you see in other European countries. It is probably too optimistic to say that by the end of 2002 the BiH banking system will have completed its transition to becoming a European type banking system. But I think most people would be surprised by how quickly the banking system will change and improve. The main things that will slow down the transition are problems in legal and regulatory frameworks in BiH that make it difficult for banks to take and use collateral for lending. This is where the reform focus now needs to be concentrated.

Title: Bosnia And Herzegovina And The Euro
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: BOSNIA & HERZEGOVINA & The EURO By Peter Nicholl, Governor of the Central Bank of Bosnia & Herzegovina (portions of this text are taken from opening comments at the European Commission Conference on the Effect of the EURO on 3rd countries) The Central Bank of Bosnia & Herzegovina, (CBBH), commenced its operations on 11, August, 1997. It is therefore still a very young institution. But it has developed well. One of the things it has done is to introduce a new legal tender currency for Bosnia & Herzegovina. The new KM currency has been well accepted. It is now used in all parts of the country, though its use is still far from equal in all parts of the country. The fact that a countrys legal tender currency is not used equally in all parts of the country may seem an unusual situation to many. But it comes about because the financial markets in Bosnia and Herzegovina could scarcly be further removed from the model now being applied in Euroland. Four currencies, the KM(BAM), DEM, YU Dinar and Croatian Kuna are still in use here. The KM is called the only domestic currency! In other words it is the only currency issued by a central bank in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is developing well and it is used all over the country, but we still have a long way to go, particularly in Herzegovina before the KM can be described as the dominant currency in the whole country. We have three Payments Bureaus, which have only just begun to integrate their operations. We have few, if any, commercial banks that operate over the whole country. If there are benefits from greater financial integration for 270 million Europeans who live in the 11 countries, the benefits for 3 and half million people here, who live in one country must be greater. The case for greater integration of the currency, payments systems and banks in Bosnia and Herzegovina is overwhelming. I think that is being increasingly recognised in Bosnia & Herzegovina. There is also a very important direct link to events in the EURO-zone. The CBBH is a currency board. What does this mean? It means the KM currency is tied to the Deutsche Mark at an exchange rate of 1:1 which is set in the CBBH Law. The CBBH is required to maintain, at least, 100% backing in foreign currency for all KM we issue and to allow full convertibility of KM into DM. The Currency Board framework has worked very well. The KM currency has remained strong and stable, even during a period of extreme turbulence in many of the worlds financial markets, and during an elections period in BiH. I believe the Currency Board structure is the only monetary policy structure that could have provided stable currency for BiH in the circumstances the country faced following the war. We have essentially tied our currency to a currency the people trust, the Deutsche Mark, and a central bank that has a long and distinguished record of sound behaviour, the Bundesbank. Now the EURO exist. Does that change our Currency Board structure and policy? The answer is no. If there is any difference, it is that the policy will be even sounder and better for BiH. First, we now specify our exchange rate as 1 KM 1 DM 0.51 EURO. We are linked to the EURO at the rate set for the DM. This exchange rate is irrevocable and can not change. Second, the stability of the EURO is the responsibility of the new European Central Bank. They have a very clear mandate to maintain price stability and I am convinced that we can have the same confidence in the ECB as we have in the Bundesbank. Thirdly, people will still be able to convert KM into DM if they so wish, as DM currency will continue to exist until January 1st 2002. Finally, the KM currency is now fixed against the currency of eleven European countries, which include most of BiHs trading partners. This should be good for both exporters to and importers from those markets as it eliminates exchange rate risk from that trade. An added benefit is the reality that before the EURO, the CBBH was limited to the choice of where to invest its foreign reserves. Under the Currency Board rules we could only place those reserves in German banks. Now with the EURO the CBBH has a choice of banks in 11 EURO countries, as long as the banks in question satisfy the CBBHs own reserve requirements. Some time between now and 2002, the CBBH Law will be amended to substitute the EURO for the DM. But, the policy will be the sameonly better, as the KM will be tied to the currency of an even bigger economy.

Title: Introduction speech at the Third Conference on Banking Sector
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: ' THE BANKING SECTOR IN BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA' CBBH CONFERENCE SARAJEVO 15 NOVEMBER 2001 OPENING ADDRESS PETER NICHOLL GOVERNOR CBBH I am very pleased to welcome you all to this Banking Sector Conference on behalf of the board and staff of the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is the third annual banking conference we have held. Each past year, I have made three general statements at the beginning of our conference. Those three statements are valid this year as well. The first is that an efficient and safe banking sector is a crucial part of a market economy. I am sure everybody here agrees with that. The second statement is that the banking sector in BH has been through many significant changes over the last year and it is in better shape today than it was when we held our last conference. Indeed, the improvements have been even more rapid over the last year than they were in the preceding year. Thats very positive. I will briefly list some of the most significant changes over the last year: The payments system has been reformed and now matches best European practice; There have been significant increases in a bank's minimum capital imposed by the banking agencies; Deposit insurance has started and is having an impact on citizens confidence in banks; More foreign banks have started operations in BH; Five banks now have branches in boost entities; And so on. But the third thing I have said in past years and have to repeat this year is that there is still a long way to go before BH has a banking sector that can play the major economic role that the banking sector plays in most other economies in Europe. We are still at an early stage in the bank reform process. At our two past conferences I have spoken mainly about bank reform and payments reform rather than about the Central Bank and the BH Currency Board arrangements. There were two reasons for this. The first was that there was so much happening in bank reform and payments reform. The second was that I thought that the Currency Board arrangements were well-understood and accepted and I didnt need to say too much about them. But there are some comments coming out recently from politicians and academics that suggest that the Currency Board is not the best monetary policy option for BH. I strongly believe that it is the best option and that to change it would have very adverse economic and social impacts. I fully understand the concerns about the state of the economy and the high level of unemployment that are causing people to examine all the policy options BH has to try and address these problems. But to change the Currency Board would be the wrong option and would make things worse rather than improve them. The first point I want to make is that Bosnia and Herzegovina does have a monetary policy. Some people are saying that to adopt a Currency Board is to give up monetary policy as an instrument of macro-economic policy. That view is wrong. Deciding to adopt a Currency Board is as much a monetary policy choice as adopting any other type of monetary policy. It is a rule-based rather than a discretionary form of monetary policy, thats true. But that is a major reason why it was chosen and is one of its strengths rather than a weakness. By choosing to adopt a Currency Board, BH decided that the aim of monetary policy will be to achieve stability  stability in the value of the local currency against the anchor currency and stability in the rate of inflation. People in BH had complete trust in the anchor currency, the DEM, because of the track record of the Central Bank of the anchor currency, the Bundesbank. The Currency Board arrangement has allowed the CBBH, a completely new institution, and the km, a completely new currency, to quickly gain some of the credibility of the Bundesbank and the DEM. The desire for stability has led to a revival of interest in Currency Boards in the 1990s when 6 or 7 were established, including the one in BH. During the 1990s a number of countries took the desire for currency stability further by fully adopting the currency of another country ( so-called Dollarisation) or introducing a new common currency over a number of countries ( the euro zone). Such areas have taken the Currency Board principle of the importance of currency stability to their furthest extent by adopting someone else's currency or a common currency. Once one adds to these countries all the countries that have during the 1990s adopted some form of inflation targeting, the overwhelming direction that monetary policy around the world has been taking over the last fifteen years is to make stability the objective of monetary policy. So the monetary policy being implemented in BH through the Currency Board is not unusual at all. What would be unusual, and would have a very adverse effect on potential foreign investors, would be a return in BH to the old discretionary type of monetary policies that have failed in many countries  and failed spectacularly in this region. I think a more apt name for that type of monetary policy is indiscretionary rather than discretionary. Maintaining the stability of the km is not a guarantee that everything in the economy will be fine. As Karl Schiller, the West German economics minister between 1996 and 1972 put it stability might not be everything, but without stability, everything else is nothing. Stability in a country's exchange rate and inflation rate are extremely important economic benefits. They allow people to plan their economic decisions ahead with more confidence. This is particularly important for investment as the economic return from any investment is spread over many years. Stability in inflation and the exchange rate are therefore critically important for investment. This is especially the case for a small country like BH that needs substantial private foreign investment. Foreign investors don't need to come to BH. They can supply the small BH market from a neighbouring country or even from their home country. Stability in inflation and the exchange rate are also extremely important for financial sector development. At present, the main risk the banks need to focus on is the credit risk of their borrowers. This is still a major problem in BH but as it is the main area of risk, it is possible to develop policies to progressively reduce it. As a consequence, we are seeing the banking sector in BH becoming more normal. But if the banks also had to worry about inflation risk and exchange rate risk, I am sure we would not have seen any significant improvements in the banking sector. Stability is also an important social benefit because it is more frequently the poor who suffer from the adverse affects of devaluation or inflation. The rich or well-connected can often finds ways around it or even ways to benefit from it. These economic benefits from stability are even more valuable in a region that has experienced extreme instability in the past. What policy makers and implementers in BH have to realise  and realise quickly  is that BH needs foreign investors more than foreign investors need BH. We therefore have to persuade them that investing here is a sensible use of their capital. In order to do this, you need to do more than say you want to attract foreign investment. As the old saying goes, actions speak louder than words. So what do the actions that have so far been taken in BH tell a potential foreign investor: The country has managed to achieve low and stable inflation and a stable exchange rate against the euro. This stability is the most positive thing BH has to attract foreign investment. The country has an improving banking sector. The reform in the banking sector has gone further and faster than reform in any other sector. Confidence is coming back, depositors are beginning to return to banks and banks are beginning to lend on more reasonable terms. Competition is real, helped by the arrival of some good foreign banks. Proportionately, foreign investment in the banking sector has been higher than in any other sector in BH. Yet we have politicians criticising banks for not lending enough and for holding so much of their liquidity outside BH. These politicians need to ask themselves why banks are still reluctant to lend more in BH. After all, banks are in the business of lending, as that is how they earn their income. But they will only lend if they can be confident that the customer will pay back the loan or, if he does not, they can go to the courts. So the key need is to get these banking risks down. The worst thing to do would be to pressure banks to ignore the real commercial risks that still exist in BH. Regulatory reform: in this area there has been little progress. In fact it may have got worse as new regulations have been introduced in many areas but few old ones have been removed. The extensive regulations allow a bureaucrat to decide how a business should operate  often in great detail  rather than the investor who is risking his money to set up the business. Legal system and courts: like most things in BH, the court system is very complex and it tends to move very slowly. For a commercial sector, including the banking sector, to be able to take business decisions and invest with confidence, it must have recourse to a legal and court system that resolves disputes quickly and fairly and upholds contracts. That is not the way people describe the BH legal system to me at present. Tax system: the tax system is also extremely complicated and the overall tax burden, if a business obeyed all its provisions, almost impossible. I have had numerous people tell me that if a business followed all the regulations and paid all the taxes and social benefits, it could not operate at a profit. That is a staggering situation. It literally forces a business to choose between operating partially in the grey economy, or going bankrupt. But what staggers me even more is that the people who tell me this seem to think that this is a normal situation. So nobody seems to be doing much about it. It is a far from normal situation and must be changed urgently. Unless the regulatory, legal and tax systems are changed, and changed quickly and substantially, BH will have a very difficult future. These problems are interrelated and have a common core  a lack of understanding of the way in which a private sector economy works and what the investment environment needs to be like to attract the level of investment that BH needs. This is where the attention of BH politicians and international consultants and advisors needs to be directed. It is this basic regulatory and microeconomic reform that will determine the future of BH. There is not one, quick policy fix that BH can adopt to get themselves out of the difficult economic situation that has built up over a long period of time. It is not that simple. Continued banking reform, accelerated regulatory reform, legal and court reform, reduction of bureaucracy, lowering of the tax burden, privatisation  there is a long list of things that need to be done. And time is running out to do them. In the meantime, the stability of the Currency Board is the most positive attribute BH has for attracting foreign investment. Given the fragility of the economic and balance of payments situations in BH at present, undermining the stability of the km by adopting some other discretionary form of monetary policy would be the best way I can think of to guarantee that BH will have an economic crisis.

Title: The First Anniversary Of The Km
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: The First Anniversary of the KM Banknote Speech notes for Peter Nicholl Governor of the Central Bank of Bosnia & Herzegovina 22, June 1999 Ministers, your excellencies, distinguished guests, members of the media and my fellow CBBH board members and staff. I would like to thank all of you for coming today to help us celebrate the first anniversary of the KM bank notes going into circulation. The KM was first put into circulation on te 22nd of June 1998. It was a surprise to me to realise that the first KM bank notes have been around for longer than that. The currency has made very good progress during its first year and so we in the CBBH feel we can celebrate its first anniversary with satisfaction and pride. The good progress it has made is all the more encouraging when one thinks back and remembers that its start as a currency was not a very auspicious one. There were a number of problems that we had to overcome. Firstly, the CBBH law said that KM coupons would be introduced within three months of the CBBH starting. But it took almost nine months to get an agreement on the designs and even then it needed the intervention of the OHR to complete the process. The only advantage of that delay was that we dropped the idea of having coupons and went straight to the bank notes. Secondly, there were some errors in the designes when the bank notes finally arrivedUnfortunately all on the RS design. Thirdly, we had problems relating to the fees that commercial banks could charge for exchanging KM and DM and some bnaks initially refused to carry out KM transactions. Fourthly, there were problems relating to the former NBBH that led to breaches of the CURRENCY BOARD. This went on for several months: much longer that it should have done. This led to delays in the acceptance of KM in the RS and in Herzegovina. Despite these early problems, the currency has become a very sound one. We have maintained more than 100% foreign reserve coverage for all our KM liabilities throughout the whole of the past year. This is the major reason why the KM has gained the trust of most of the people and it is being increasingly accepted and used by both local people and the international community. There are many signs of the growing acceptance and use of the KM over the last year. One broad indicator is that the size of the CBBH banlance sheet has grown from around KM 150 MILLION a year ago to KM 340 MILLION at the end of May 1999, a growth of 127% in a zear. As a CURRENCY BOARD, the main source of growth of our balance sheet is people and banks buying KM with convertible foreign currency. That is what they have been doing. The support of the international community has been an important factor in this. A number of the international organisations representated here today for this ceremony made great efforts to have their dispursements converted to KM and to pay their staff in KM. I want to thank them for their support. We get daily figures of our sales and purchases of KM in our four offices and I look at those figures most days. It is almost as if the governments, the banks and the public have been giving the CBBH a birthday present because the net sales last week ( 14th18th June) were the highest for a long time. We sold nearly 15 million KM last week. The KM is certainly not yet the sole currency in BiH or even the main currency in all parts of the country, but we can claim that by the end of its first year, it had become the dominant currency when one looks at the whole of BiH. The DEM, the Croatian Kuna and the Yugoslavian Dinar are still used to varying degrees. But there are a number of steps the entity governments either have taken or have said they will soon take that will further promote the use of the KM and reduce the roles of these other currencies. For example, the RS government has already taken the DEM out of their domestic payments bureau and the Federation BiH parliament has before it a draft law that will in the near future take the DEM and the Kuna out of their payments bureau. This was supposed to have happened by June 30th. Unfortunately, this targhet date is unlikely to be achieved and the delay is a concern. The CBBH is working with the Federation BiH ministry of finance, the bnaking agency and the payments bureaus on the technical steps necessary to make this happen very soon. The Yugoslavian Dinar has been substancially replaced by the KM in pricing, currency, bank deposits, and domestic payments in the RS over the last 6 months. The RS government is also making an increased proportion of their wage, benefit and service payments in KM. I believe the proportion is currently 70% as the RS government gains further access to foreign exchange funds, their stated intention is to raise the KM proportion in their payments to 100%. The Federation BiH prime minister and minister of finance also agreed at the May Federation Forum to move to paying all their wage, benefits and services in KM and to require all Federation taxes to be paid in KM. So far these measures have note been actioned by the Federation government. I urge them to do so promptly. I do not believe there are any good reasons why these steps have been delayed. With the steps that have either been taken or are promised by the entity governments, we should see continued strong growth in the use of KM over the next year. The KM should in its second year in circulation become the dominant currency in use in all parts of the country, including Heryegovina. Further expansion of the use of KM is essential for economic integration within the country. Already inter-entity trade is growing and the ability to settle transactions between the entities in a stable KM is one of the main factors that is helping this happen. The existance of a stable KM tied through the DEM to the EURO also means that BiH has a stable exchange rate with an enormous European trading yone of eleven countries. This will be very helpful for increasing foreign trade and foreign investment in BiH, both prerequisites for further economic development. The CBBH has not achieved the success of the KM alone. It has been a joint effort of many people and groups. I want to thank some of them now. Firstly, the French government for funding the printing of our bank notes and the French company Oberthur for assisting in the design process and printing the bank notes. Secondly, I want to publicly thank the politicians of BiH for the strong support they have given the CURRENCY BOARD framework we operate under. This support is very important for the success of the CURRENCY BOARD and for the stability of the KM. Thirdly, the international community for assisting us in many ways. One of themost important has been using the KM themselves. There are now only a few examples of foreign agencies in BiH not using the KM. I hope the remaining few will get on board and use the KM in the near future. I would particularly like to thank the IMF for all the advice they have given the CBBH both before and after its establishment and the OHR for their strong support at crucial times in the process of introducing and promoting the KM. I feel it is a good sign for the CBBH and for BiH that we feel we can promote and expand the use of KM now without the need to go frequently to the OHR to get decisions taken. However, their earlier support and decisiveness was crucial for the establishment of the KM. I also want to thank the BiH media. They have given the story of the KM a lot of publicityand most of it has been favourable publicity. Part of the credit for the high amount of public knowledge of and support for the KM therefore goes to you for the telling of the KM story so well. I also want to thank the payments bureaus in BiH who have been our agents in distributing and storing the KM around the country. The CBBH has only four offices and we have therefore relied on the payments bureaus to provide quick and safe access to the KM over the whole country. They have done a good job Finally I want to thank the Board and staff of the CBBH. The successful introduction of the KM is the most obvious achievement of the CBBH over the past year. It is something we can all take pride in. But it is not the only thing we have done. We have at the same time set up four offices, employed 160 staff, set up our accounting and other internal policies, opened reserve accounts for all the banks in the country, started an inter/bank clearing mechanism, published an economic bulliten, invested our foreign reserves and so on. In short, we have successfully established an institution that is working well in all its operations. I want to publically thank all the staff for the excellent work they have done, and the Governing Board for the constructive way in which it has operated and for the sound guideance it has given the CBBH. I have already mentioned some critical steps that the entity governments need to take to continue the expansion of use of the KM. I want to conclue with a few comments on issues the CBBH will work on during the next year. In the currency area, we will probably introduce KM 1 & 2 coins. We are considering having a competition to produce the designs for these new coins. We will also need to consider how we should respond to the forthcoming disappearance of the DEM bank notes, though this is not yet urgent. The major issue for the next year will be integration and reform of the banking and payments systems in BiH. I will not go into the details of what will be involved in those reforms as I think they are quite well known and today we are here to talk about the KM. However, I do take every opportunity to stress that it is critically important for BiH to carry out reform of the financial sector and develop a modern, marketbased financial system. The introduction of a sound and stable domestic currency, the KM, is one important step in developing a strong financial system. We will maintain the soundness of the CURRECY BOARDthat is our pledge to the people of BiH. They have shown that they have confidence in the KM by increasing their use of it over the past year. We will make sure that they can continue to have confidence in the stability and convertibility of the KM. I will now ask each of my three vice-governors to say a few words on particular aspects of the KM and the CURRENCY BOARD. -30- PAGE 1 PAGE 4

Title: Role of Currency Board in Monetary policy
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: Jure Pelivan Member of the Governing Board of the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina Sarajevo, 11 April 2003 Paper for discussion at the Conference on the subject: Role of Currency Board in monetary policy Comments on practice in Bosnia and Herzegovina Introduction Bosnia and Herzegovina is a specific country when compared to other transition countries. In the time of dissolution of the former SFRY, which formally and legally commenced in the second half of 1991, out of the 6 former republics, it went through large difficulties. It experienced a war conflict which resulted in enormous human and material losses and devastation. The available data show that more than 200.000 persons died and were killed or disappeared in the war in the period from May 1992 to November 1995. The demographic structure of population has been completely changed. Out of the total of 4 million and 370 thousand of citizens, the number recorded at the official census in 1991, around 2 million citizens left their homes and places of their residency during the war, out of fear or because they had been forced to do so, and they either went to another countries or moved within Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the post-war return process, there have been serious problems reflected in a slow reconstruction of family houses and apartments, which had been to a great extent destroyed or devastated, and also very difficult circumstances for sustainable living. There are estimates which say that around 500.000 people are still waiting to return. A large part of the economic facilities and infrastructure have been destroyed or devastated. Direct damages in economic facilities are estimated to exceed USD 50 billion, which is also the approximate amount of indirect damages. Fortunately, the war conflict is behind us. It consequences are being dealt with, with significant help of the international community and the help of a number of friendly countries, which was promised and implemented in various forms, through humanitarian donations, non-repayable funds and favourable loans for reconstruction and development of economy in the value of USD 5 billion. This support has been decreasing lately, but it is still considerable. Bosnia and Herzegovina and its citizens highly appreciate of it and do not forget it. For purpose of this discussion, it is useful to start from the General Peace Agreement for Bosnia and Herzegovina which was reached in November 1995. This Agreement set out the arrangements for its implementation. In Annex IV  Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina set out a specific internal political and territorial organization, saying that BiH will consist of the two entities (those being the Federation of BiH and Republika Srpska). Article VII defines that the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina will exist, which is to be the sole authority for issuing currency and conducting monetary policy in entire BiH. The competence of the Central Bank is defined by the Parliamentary Assembly, however, it has been regulated that in the first six years, it shall not extend loans by creation of money and shall function as Currency Board in that respect. After that period, the Parliamentary Assembly may assign that power to the Central Bank. Law on the Central Bank of BiH On the basis of this principle, the Law on the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina was adopted in the Bi H Parliament on 20 June 1997, and the Bank commenced its operations on 11 August 1997. The Central Bank is fully independent in performance of its functions as set out under this law. Its basic tasks and objectives, just to mention some, are the following: -to define and control implementation of monetary policy of Bosnia and Herzegovina; -to issue and put into circulation and withdraw from circulation banknotes and coins and also purchase and sale of the local currency  Convertible Marka against EUR at the fixed exchange rate: 1 EUR 1,955830 KM (before 31 December 2001  1 DEM 1 KM); -to maintain stability of the local currency, so that its monetary liabilities (monetary base) should never exceed the equivalent amount (denominated in KM ) of reserves in a foreign convertible currency (EUR) and to manage the foreign exchange reserves in a safe and profitable way; -to guarantee the convertibility of the local currency, by means of free purchase and sale of the local currency to banks under the permanent fixed ratio to EUR as defined by law; -to help or establish and maintain appropriate payment and settlement systems and to carry out settlement of payment transactions in the local currency among banks, by means of electronic system gyro clearing and RTGS; -to coordinate activities of the banking agencies, in charge of licensing and supervision of banks; -to receive deposits of BiH institutions and deposits of the Entities and other public institutions, in case they decide so, and to run banks' reserve accounts, including the control of fulfillment of bank's reserve requirement (10% of the amount of their deposits) The law regulates that the Central Bank cannot be engaged in the operations at the money market, including also any kind of securities. It can work as a banker and fiscal agent of Bosnia and Herzegovina and some public agencies, provided that no transaction is used as financial aid, including loans, for or in favour of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Central Bank, its assets, property and income, and also its operations and transactions, are exempt from all taxes and customs duties. Implementation of the currency board arrangement It is correct to state that in the practice by this moment, the Central Bank has insured continuity in the implementation of the Currency Board arrangement, with a small exception in the first months of 1997, when, due to technical mistakes, immobilization of state institution deposits was not carried out, which at that moment was not covered by convertible currency (DEM), but even that mistake was removed in the beginning of 1998. The actual continuity is confirmed by the data shown in the enclosed table 1, so, apart from the mentioned exception, foreign assets (the reserves managed by the Central Bank) were always higher that its monetary liabilities (monetary base). Payment Operations It is interesting to mention that in the war period from May 1992 to the end of 1999, in the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were three parallel currency areas and payment bureaus. In that time, in each of these areas, in the internal payment system, several currencies were used as means of payment: in one area there were BH Dinar and DEM, in the other there were Croatian Kuna and DEM and in the third one there were YU Dinar and DEM. Upon enforcement of the Law on the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina, currency BH Dinar was converted into KM in gyro transactions, however, BH Dinar banknotes were kept in the circulation until KM banknotes were printed, i.e. until the end of June 1998. The law also regulated that other currencies which had been used in circulation before the enforcement of the law (DEM, Croatian Kuna and YU Dinar) could be used after that time limit. However, those other currencies were excluded from the internal payment system in the end of September 1999. Since that time, Convertible Marka has been the only legal tender in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The reform of the payment system has been carried out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the internal payment system has been transferred from payment bureaus to commercial banks and the Central Bank. The new payment system became operative on 05 January 2001. Payment system operations are efficiently performed through the payment systems, RTGS (real time gross settlement) for settlement of large value transactions and Gyro Clearing for a large volume of small value transactions. Banks have the possibility to carry out settlement in gyro clearing three times a day. As of 31 December 2002, 41 commercial bank and the Central Bank were included in payment system. During the two years of operations of the new payment system, over 27 million of transactions in the value of KM 39,3 billion were carried out. 590.313 transactions (2%) in the value of KM 23,2 billion (59%) were carried out through RTGS, and 26.852.748 transactions (98%) in the value of KM 16,1 billion (41%) were carried out through the gyro clearing. The mentioned data reflect only the part of payment transactions performed among banks by means of electronic processing in the Central Bank. In addition to these transactions, a great number has been performed in each bank among its clients. For purpose of illustration, 24,5 million transactions in the value of KM 26,2 billion were carried out in 2002 within the banks. In 2002, activities were carried out for improvement of payment systems, particularly in the field of card operations. The Central Bank has officially become an agent in processing of card operations. In the previous two years of payment transaction processing, there were no delays. To the common satisfaction of clients and banks, it is a general impression that internal payment system reform has been carried out successfully, its result being significant acceleration in money circulation and the increase of the degree of liquidity. Commercial Banking Sector Commercial banking sector, together with almost all the other sectors of the financial system, is based on legislation of the two entities (the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska), and has been regulated on the basis of the law on two banking agencies which issue licenses for establishment and operations of banks and also bank supervision. However, it is correct to say that principles and methodology for their operations are harmonised. Since the establishment of the banking agencies, a considerable progress has been made in banking supervision, good management, constant and effective technical assistance, and the increasing protection of the agencies from the unproductive political influence. The Central Bank also undertakes regular activities in coordination of the work of the agencies with purpose of better exchange of information and closer cooperation in banking supervision between the entity agencies. It should be particularly stressed that by adopting the Law and the beginning of operations in 2002 of the Deposit Insurance Agency at the state level, a significant contribution has been made in further development and strengthening of confidence of clients-depositors of banks. By now, even 10 banks have concluded contracts with this agency on insurance of their deposits. In 2002, further progress has been made in consolidation of the banking sector in two directions. One was merger of banks (through merging or acquisition of smaller banks by more developed banks). The other form of activities was focused on privatization in the banking sector. A very good progress in accomplishment of these objectives is illustrated by the data in the enclosed table 2 and 3. Speaking of bank privatization, it can be reliably assumed that this process will be completed in 2003, and further gradual merging of banks is expected and simultaneously their increasing presence in all parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina through a wider network of organizational units (branches and offices) The process of bank merger results in a faster increase of credit and business potential by supply of larger range of services to clients. The increased presence of a number of foreign banks is evident. They purchase ownership shares of the local-earlier founders and bring additional credit potential. Specifically, the share of foreign resident banks in the stock capital of banks in the end of 2002, at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina, amounts to 6%, whereas the share of the state capital was reduced from 47% in 2000 to only 10% in the end of 2002. SUMMARY Results and suggestions In the operations of the Central Bank of BiH by now, in the previous almost six years, currency board has been fully implemented, in the way that its foreign exchange assets (foreign reserves managed by it) have always been higher than its liabilities (monetary base) denominated in the local currency  KM, which it put into circulation. Furthermore, net foreign assets have been increasing year after year. By applying currency board consistently, the Central Bank has not extended one single loan, or any kind of money lending to banks or the state bodies, i.e. their institutions. Therefore, all the provisions of the existing Law on the Central Bank of BiH have been consistently applied. It is undoubted that citizens, economy and all the others in BiH have expressed their full confidence in the local currency, as it is convertible, i.e. freely interchangeable for all the other convertible currencies, at the fixed exchange rate as set out by law. It can be reliably concluded that the stability of the local currency in a longer period has had an important role in maintaining stable prices at the local market. It is confirmed by the data on retail prices recording a downward trend, so their weighted level at BiH level in 2002 recorded the increase of only 0,4% compared to 2001. It is true that some constant increase of industrial production and gross domestic product (GDP) is maintained, which is a result of complex factors. However, it is undoubted that this trend is to a great extent due to a very low base which existed in the post war period. This can be documented with the data that in the end of 2001, according to the official statistics, GDP per capita was only slightly above the half which was reached in 1990. The economic development achieved in the previous six years is unsatisfactory according to the relevant criteria, but the trend of production and the total operation is still obvious. It is accomplished by using local resources and significant financial credit support and donations for specific purposes. The problem is that reduction of foreign help in the years to come is announced, and the local financial-credit potentials are not sufficient for acceleration of the economic development. In addition, the ratio of trade with foreign countries is quite unfavorable, which is reflected in the increasing foreign trade deficit. The fact that a considerable part of current potential in banks is allocated to credit the spending and the smaller part is allocated for development of production is concerning. Naturally, banks behave according to the market principles, and allocate loans to those users who perform their obligations more regularly. However, through measures of economic policy and by insuring a more effective legal and executive procedure, it is necessary to provide for appropriate instruments which will help that banks find more interest in allocating a bigger part of their potential to support production for which there are significant natural resources. It means that the total economic stability can be achieved by complex measures of economic policy, which will result in acceleration of growth of production for exports and more favorable environment for direct foreign investment in our economy, which includes both the interest of foreign partners and domestic economy. Finally, there is a provision in the Law on the Central Bank of BiH saying that Parliamentary Assembly, after expiry of the 6 year period, may decide to authorize the Central Bank to have some possibility of extending loans. The law includes a provision on the fixed exchange rate between the local currency and EUR, without time distinction. There arises a question if the time has come to suggest the change of these provisions to Parliamentary Assembly of BiH. We are obliged to remind that official representatives of the IMF are suggesting, and we can say, conditioning, the preservation of the currency board, with adequate explanations. We should also take into account that high state officials have expressed their support to such attitude of the IMF. Management and governing structures of the Central Bank also have the attitude that in the particular situation we should persist in the opinion that the circumstances are not such to enable decision on creation of money by the Central Bank without adequate foreign exchange coverage in the anchor convertible currency EUR. Such attitude of the management bodies of the Central Bank, in my opinion, does not restrict the possibility of performing serious research and analyses for purpose of more complete usage of some possibilities, such as: -more rational use of available potentials in banks which make possible the credit multiplication, which is currently in coefficient up to 1,5 or slightly above in relation to the monetary base (monetary liabilities) of the Central Bank; -consideration of some favorable conditions by the CBBH in the form of acknowledging compensation to banks for transfer of a part of their foreign exchange deposits for the local currency; -establishment of a more active cooperation with the first class foreign banks for their support to their clients for bigger engagement of direct investments or allocation of acceptable loans, from the countries with which we have some level of foreign trade and other cooperation. In any case, I believe this is not a taboo, which could not be discussed for purpose of using some possibilities also within the implementation of the currency board arrangement.

Title: Speech on the opening of the Days of BH Finances
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: DAYS OF BH FINANCE BANJALUKA, MARCH 8TH AND MAY 9, 2008 SPEECH BY BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR KEMALA KOZARIC Dear ladies and gentlemen, I am extremely pleased to have the opportunity to address you today and welcome you to the third bh fair. Finance. I use this occasion to express my satisfaction with the fact that this event gains importance, qualityin the number of participants every year. I am sincerely convinced that in the foreseeable future this event will become a reference, not only in the region, but beyond. This year's event is called "Financial Stability 96 Reality or Illusion", which was not chosen by accident. Namely, financial stability is now the most important area of study of financial experts around the world, and the major financial crises affecting even the most developed countries have led to crises and many problems in financial institutions that we until recently considered invulnerable. Although many theories can be found in academic circles about the causes, consequences and ways of preventing crises, everyone agrees on one thing, which is that without synergy all parts of the financial sector, financial stability cannotbe achieved or preserved. The same rules apply to Bosnia and Herzegovina, which until now has been spared the effects of the world's financial crises. This, of course, did not happen because our state has a great mechanism for crisis prevention, but because of the happy circumstances that the big players in the regional banking market, who founded or privatised banks in our state, were not exposed in the markets where the crisis occurred. Precisely because it is necessary to work continuously to develop co-operation between parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina's financial sector, and that major crises can happen almost without notice, I am extremely pleased to see representatives of all parts of bh at this event. financial sector. In today's turbulent environment, the question of "can there be a crisis" can be freely replaced with the question "when will there be a crisis". Each country's financial stability is measuredin the same way that it resistspotential external shackles and responds with its own resources in the short term. Our goal is to act preventively in Bosnia and Herzegovina as well, and to recognize potential risks on time and to ensurethe stability of the entire financial sector. The central bank is certainly one of the pillars of financial stability in the state, and bosnia and Herzegovina's Central Bank, consistently implementing monetary policy and responsibly executing its functions, has contributed to maintaining monetary stability as one of the basic preconditions for financial stability. Also, the pro-eczemawe have launched, such as Registra loans and Registra transaction accounts, have given new tools to commercial banks, which enable them to better assess customer bonuses and safer placements. Nevertheless, we are aware that financial stability can only be achieved by synergy of all parts of the financial sector in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I hope that today's presentations will help better understand the very concept and importance of financial stability for all of us, and that they will also semi-set out certain initiatives to improve co-operation in this field. Before I finish, let me give you a few more information about today's sessions.
text_original: DANI BH FINANSIJA BANJALUKA, 8. I 9. MAJ 2008. GODINE GOVOR GUVERNERA CENTRALNE BANKE BOSNE I HERCEGOVINE KEMALA KOZARIA Potovane dame i gospodo, Izuzetno mi je zadovoljstvo to danas imam priliku da vam se obratim i poelim dobrodolicu na trei po redu sajam bh. finansija. Koristim se ovom prilikom da izrazim zadovoljstvo injenicom da ova manifestacija svake godine dobija na znaaju, kvalitetu i broju uesnika. Iskreno sam uvjeren u to da e u dogledno vrijeme ova manifestacija postati referentna, ne samo u regionu, nego i ire. Ovogodinja manifestacija odrava se pod nazivom Finansijska stabilnost  stvarnost ili iluzija, koji nije odabran sluajno. Naime, finansijska stabilnost predstavlja danas najvanije podruje prouavanja finansijskih strunjaka irom svijeta, a velike finansijske krize koje pogaaju ak i najrazvijenije drave dovele su do kriza i velikog broja problema i u finansijskim institucijama koje smo donedavno smatrali neranjivima. Iako se u akademskim krugovima mogu nai mnoge teorije o uzrocima, posljedicama i nainima predupreenja kriza, svi se slau u jednom, a to je da se bez sinergije svih dijelova finansijskog sektora ne moe postii niti ouvati finansijska stabilnost. Ista pravila vae i za Bosnu i Hercegovinu, koja je do sada bila poteena efekata svjetskih finansijskih kriza. To se, naravno, nije desilo zato to naa drava ima sjajan mehanizam za prevenciju kriza, nego zbog sretne okolnosti da veliki igrai na regionalnom bankarskom tritu, koji su osnovali ili privatizirali banke u naoj dravi, nisu bili izloeni na tritima na kojima se kriza desila. Upravo zbog injenica da je neophodno kontinuirano raditi na razvoju saradnje izmeu dijelova finansijskog sektora Bosne i Hercegovine, te da se velike krize mogu desiti gotovo bez najave, izuzetno mi je drago to na ovoj manifestaciji vidim predstavnike svih dijelova bh. finansijskog sektora. U dananjem turbulentnom okruenju, pitanje da li moe doi do krize slobodno moemo zamijeniti sa pitanjem kada e doi do krize. Finansijska stabilnost svake zemlje mjeri se sposobnou iste da se usjeno odupre eventualnim eksternim okovima i u kratkom roku reaguje sopstvenim resursima. Na cilj je da i u Bosni i Hercegovini djelujemo preventivno, te prepoznamo potencijalne rizike na vrijeme i na organizovan nain ouvamo stabilnost cijelog finansijskog sektora. Centralna banka je sigurno jedan od stubova finansijske stabilnosti u dravi, a Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine je, dosljedno sprovodei monetarnu politiku i odgovorno izvravajui svoje funkcije, maksimalno pridonijela odravanju monetarne stabilnosti kao jednog od osnovnih preduslova finansijske stabilnosti. Takoe, projekti koje smo pokrenuli, poput Registra kredita i Registra transakcijskih rauna, dali su nove alate komercijalnim bankama, koji im omoguavaju bolju procjenu boniteta klijenata i sigurnije plasmane. Ipak, svjesni smo da se finansijska stabilnost moe postii samo sinergijskim djelovanjem svih dijelova finansijskog sektora u Bosni i Hercegovini. Nadam se da e dananje prezentacije pomoi boljem razumijevanju samog pojma i znaaja finansijske stabilnosti za sve nas, te da e poluiti i odreene inicijative za unapreenje saradnje na ovom polju. Prije nego zavrim, dopustite mi jo da vam dam nekoliko informacija o dananjim sesijama.

Title: "Deposit insurance in transitioning countries - Has it really strengthened the banking system? "; European Forum on Deposit Insurance
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: GOVERNOR KEMAL KOZARIC WELCOME ADDRESS TO THE EUROPEAN FORUM OF DEPOSIT INSURERS DEPOSIT INSURANCE IN TRANSITIONING COUNTRIES. HAS IT REALLY STRENGTHENED THE BANKING SYSTEM? DECEMBER 8TH AND 9TH 2005 SARAJEVO, HOTEL HOLIDAY INN HOTEL SARAJEVO BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA LADIES AND GENTLEMAN, I AM PLEASED TO HAVE THIS OPPORTUNITY TO TALK TO YOU TODAY AND WARMLY WELCOME YOU ALL TO THIS IMPORTANT AND INTERESTING FORUM. THE QUESTION WE SHELL ATTEMPT TO ANSWER TODAY IS HAS DEPOSIT INSURANCE REALLY STRENGTHENED THE BANKING SYSTEM IN BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA AS A COUNTRY IN TRANSITION. VERY CLEARLY AND OBVIOUSLY THE ANSWER IS YES, DEPOSIT INSURANCE IS ONE OF SEVERAL VERY IMPORTANT FACTORS, WHICH HAVE INFLUENCED AND CONTINUES TO INFLUENCE THE STRENGTHENING OF THE BANKING SECTOR IN THE COUNTRY. DEPOSIT INSURANCE PLAYED A CRUCIAL ROLE IN HELPING TO RESTORE TRUST AND INCREASE THE CONFIDENCE OF CITIZENS IN OUR BANKS. THE DEPOSIT INSURANCE STRUCTURE IN BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA IS WELL DESIGNED, TOO. THE DEPOSIT INSURANCE AGENCY HAS STRICTLY AND PRECISELY DEFINED THE CRITERIA FOR MEMBERSHIP AND PERHAPS MORE IMPORTANTLY HAS MAINTAINED IT SO THAT IT HAS BEEN CONSISTENT IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ITS RULES AND REGULATIONS. ALSO, THERE ARE OTHER REFORMS THAT HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED IN THE BANKING SECTOR DURING THE PAST DECADE, WHICH HAVE, ALONG WITH DEPOSIT INSURANCE, HELPED TO DEVELOP THE SECTOR. I WILL LIST SOME OF THE MOST IMPORTANT ONES. FIRST OF ALL, THE ARRIVAL OF SOUND FOREIGN BANKS BRINGING NEW CAPITAL, IDEAS AND NEW PRODUCTS TO THIS REGION, BUT MORE IMPORTANTLY INCREASING COMPETITION IN THIS SECTOR. THEIR ARRIVAL HAS ALSO HELPED RESTORE CONFIDENCE IN THE BANKS. THESE BANKS WERE THE FIRST TO CROSS ENTITY LINES, UNIFYING THE TERRITORY OF BIH AND THE ECONOMIC SPACE OF THE COUNTRY. SECONDLY, AN INCREASE IN THE STARTING CAPITAL TO 15 MILLION KM, HAS STIMULATED BANK AQUSITIONS AND FORCED SOME OF THE SMALLER BANKS TO MERGE, REDUCING THE TOTAL NUMBER OF BANKS IN THE COUNTRY. TODAY WE HAVE 33 BANKS. THE PROCESS OF REDUCTION IN THE NUMBER OF BANKS WILL BE CONTINUED, AS THE ECONOMIC SPACE OF BIH IS TOO SMALL EVEN FOR 33 BANKS. ALSO, GLOBALIZATION IS A MAJOR FEATURE OF THE PRESENT STAGE OF THE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT WORLDWIDE. WE SEE THE SAME PROCESS CONTINUING TO HAPPEN IN BIH AND WE CAN SAY THAT IN BIH WE ALREADY HAVE A EUROPEAN TYPE BANKING SYSTEM. THE REFORM OF THE BIH BANKING SECTOR HAS GONE FURTHER AND FASTER THEN REFORM IN ANY OTHER SECTOR OF THE ECONOMY. THIRD THE ISSUE I WANT TO MENTION, WHICH IS RELATED TO THE SECOND ONE, IS BANK PRIVATIZATION. ALTHOUGH THERE ARE STILL FIVE STATE OWNED BANKS IN THE COUNTRY, TOTALING A 5% MARKET SHARE, I FEEL FREE TO SAY THAT THE PRIVATIZATION OF THIS SECTOR IS SUCCESSFULLY FINALIZED. PRIVATISATION OF THE BANKING SECTOR HAS ATTRACTED SIGNIFICANT FOREIGN INVESTMENT AND IT IS A GOD EXAMPLE THAT IT IS POSSIBLE TO RUN BUSINESS AND MAKE PROFIT IN BIH. FORTH, THE PAYMENTS SYSTEM UNDERWENT FUNDAMENTAL REFORM. IT HAS BEEN OPERATING IN THE CBBH SINCE JANUARY 5, 2001. WE FEEL VERY PROUD OF THE FACT THAT REFORM WENT VERY SMOOTHLY AND WE WILL CONTINUE TO WORK WITH THE COMMERCIAL BANKS TO CONSTANTLY IMPROVE THE PAYMENT SYSTEM IN BIH. THE FIFTH REASON IS INTEREST RATES REDUCTION. THE AVERAGE SHORT-TERM LOAN INTEREST RATE IS 9.90%, WHILE THE AVERAGE LONG TERM LOAN RATE IS 7.90%. THESE RATES CAN STILL BE CONSIDERED QUITE HIGH, BUT WE ARE CERTAIN THAT THE POSITIVE TREND OF RATE REDUCTION SHALL BE CONTINUED. AS I HAVE ALREADY MENTIONED THERE ARE OTHER REFORMS WHICH HAVE STIMULATED SIGNIFICANT INCREAS OF THE RESTORATION OF CONFIDENCE IN THE BANKS. ALTHOUGH THE ECONOMIC SITUATION IN THE COUNTRY IS NOT VERY GOOD, STILL THOSE WHO ARE ABLE TO SAVE DEPOSIT THEIR SAVINGS IN THE BANKING SECTOR, A RELIABLE PARTNER FOR SAVINGS... THIS IS A GOOD OPPORTUNITY TO REMEMBER HOW IMPORTANT SAVINGS IS FOR THE PROSPERITY OF THE COUNTRY AND ITS CITIZENS. GROWTH IN DOMESTIC SAVINGS WILL BE A NECESSARY PRECONDITION FOR FURTHER ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. IN THAT SENSE, INCREASED DEPOSITS BY CITIZENS SHOULD STIMULATE FASTER RECOVERY FOR THE COUNTRY IN GENERAL WHICH BY ITSELF WILL INCREASE THE LEVEL OF OVERALL BUSINESS, MORE JOBS AND A BETTER STANDARD OF LIVING. BY THE END OF SEPTEMBER 2005, INDIVIDUAL PRIVATE DEPOSITS IN COMMERCIAL BANKS OF BIH TOTALED KM 3.9 BILLION AND GREW BY 30.2% COMPARED TO THE END OF SEPTEMBER 2004. TO CONCLUDE, THE DEPOSIT INSURANCE STRUCTURE IN THE COUNTRY IS A POSITIVE EXAMPLE OF AN EFFICIENT AND EFFECTIVE TOOL AT THE STATE LEVEL, WHICH FACILITATES IMPROVEMENT OF THE ENTIRE BANKING SECTOR. I TRULY HOPE THAT THIS PRINCIPAL WILL BE FOLLOWED WITH THE BANKING SUPERVISION FUNCTION SO THAT IT WILL FINALLY BE TAKEN TO THE CENTRAL BANK OF BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA IN THE INTEREST OF THE CITIZENS AND DEPOSITORS OF THIS COUNTRY. THERE IS AN OLD SAYING IN THIS COUNTRY, WHICH GOES LIKE THIS: IT TAKES MORE SKILLFULNESS TO SAVE THEN TO EARN. SAVING IS WISDOM OF SPENDING, BUT IN ORDER TO MAKE THIS SLOGAN FEASIBLE, IT IS NECESSARY TO IMPROVE THE ECONOMIC SITUATION IN THE COUNTRY AND THE STANDARD OF LIVING FOR EACH AND EVERY CITIZEN HAS TO BE MUCH BETTER. BEST WISHES FOR THE REST OF THE FORUM, WHICH CAN ALREADY BE ACKNOWLEDGED AS A SUCCESSFUL ONE AS NO POLITICIAN HAD BEEN INVITED NOR IS ATTENDING THIS DISTINGUISHED FORUM. ALL THE PEOPLE PRESENT HERE ARE PROFESSIONALS AND EXPERTS IN THIS FIELD AND THEREFORE DISCUSSION WILL BE RELEVANT AND I HOPE VERY FRUITFUL. ALLOW ME WISH YOU A VERY GOOD STAY IN BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA. I HOPE THAT YOU WILL MANAGE TO SEE THIS BEAUTIFUL COUNTRY IN A DIFFERENT LIGHT, BETTER THEN THE ONE THAT DOMINATES THE MINDS OF FOREIGNERS WHO HAVE NEVER VISITED BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA BEFORE. WE ARE WELL AWARE OF THE NECESSITY TO WORK MORE AND MORE ON THE PROMOTION OF OUR COUNTRY IN ORDER TO IMPROVE ITS IMAGE AND TO PRESENT IT IN A RATHER MORE OBJECTIVE MANNER. PLEASE BE OUR AMBASSADORS ABROAD, IN YOUR HOME COUNTRIES AND HELP US TO START PROMOTING A BETTER IMAGE OF THIS COUNTRY; ONE IT TRULY DESERVES. AN IMAGE OF POSITIVE CHANGE, GROWTH AND STABILITY. THANK YOU FOR YOUR ATTENTION.

Title: Microfinances in BH - Speech at the Ceremonial Session of the Association of Micro-crediting Organizations of BH
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: MICRO FINANCES IN BIH SPEECH DELIVERED BY GOVERNOR OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF BH KEMAL KOZARI AT THE CEREMONIAL SESSION OF THE ASSOCIATION OF MICRO-CREDITING ORGANIZATIONS OF BH SARAJEVO, DECEMBER 8, 2005 If we say that the banking sector is the best organized part of the financial sector and that it is a successful story in BH, then the micro financial sector is a continuation of that story. The micro financial sector has proved to be very useful and effective in transition countries, because the micro financial organizations with their lending instruments are focused on the categories which can not fulfill the criteria of commercial banks and have no access to the banking sector. The micro financial sector is becoming increasingly important in the world, therefore it does not keep its activities only on micro credits, but it expands its operations to the providing of consulting services in management and improvement of business of its clients. This sector develops and improves the principles and standards of operations in order to achieve efficiency and productivity. In order to achieve transparency and to observe the performance of the micro financial sector, the set of joint indicators has been established, to monitor the situation in this area and the influence on financial sector and overall economy. These indicators include management, information, risks, activities (products and services), financing, efficiency, profitability and solidarity. Micro financial sector in BH is developing at an accelerated pace, thanks to the investments made by the World Bank, the USAID, the EBRD and other donors within the Local Initiatives Project. Micro crediting in BH has been introduced as a support to small enterprises which have difficulties to access the banking loans and the banks do not have sufficient interest for such kind of clients. In 2004, eight partnership micro credit organizations had 87.861 active clients with the active portfolio in the amount over KM 193 million. Taking into account that in 2004 these organizations extended 90.073 credits in the amount of KM 282 million, as well as that the average amount of credit was KM 2.300 and that there were 88.000 active clients, and the indicator that one active credit (client's micro business) employs 2, 15 people on the average, which results in the number of 280.000 people employed by micro credits, it clearly shows the importance of this sector. The question arises how many of such employees have been registered and how many of them have remained in informal sector. Concluding with September 30 this year, the amount of extended micro credits achieved KM 315 million and the total number of extended micro credits achieved 112.000 with the average credit amount of KM 2.053 and 134.745 active clients (micro businesses). The Central Bank supports the establishment of the systemic solutions in this area, considering their importance for development of small businesses, as well as the appropriate supervision of their work. The current solutions of supervision of micro credit organizations (the Ministry for Labor and Social Issues is authorized in one entity, while the Finance Ministry is authorized in the other entity) are not adjusted to financial systems and they are not viable. In order to provide appropriate supervision, the new law provides for a solution which will be adjusted to and consistent with the supervision as in the banking system. According to the proposed solutions, the institution which performs the supervision of commercial banks is also in charge of the supervision of operations of micro credit organizations. We truly hope that quite soon that institution will be the Central Bank. New law makes possible the transformation of micro credit organizations into the commercial legal entities in order to create self-sustainable micro credit organizations. Draft Law provides for the existence of two basic forms of micro credit organizations  micro credit foundations as the unprofitable organization (which will have an emphasized social role and it will be a socially useful organization) and micro credit associations, as the profitable organization, and they can be organized as the association with limited responsibility or as the shareholder company. The organized system and supervision in this area will require a strict adherence to the defined rules of operations, so tendencies similar to those in the banking sector can be expected to take place in this area. It is expected that micro credit organizations will merge and that some micro credit organizations will take the positions of leaders. In order to provide the operating of this sector on sound and stable bases, it is necessary to increase the required initial capital (KM 50.000 for foundations and KM 500.000 for micro credit organizations). Since the micro financial sector with its portfolio of around KM 300 million has a significant position in the overall financial system, the Central Bank supports the reform of the macro financial sector and it is involved in this process with purpose of achieving overall financial stability as well as positive influence on macroeconomic trends in BH. Therefore, the CBBH clearly supports the reforms in this area and it will do so in the future as well, because this sector is important in the overall financial system.

Title: Opening address at the Constituent Assembly of the F/BH Banking Association
CentralBank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: GOVERNOR PETER NICHOLL OPENING ADDRESS AT THE CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY OF THE F/BIH BANKING ASSOCIATION 30 JANUARY 2003 CENTRAL BANK OF BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA I AM PLEASED TO HAVE THIS OPPORTUNITY TO TALK TO YOU TODAY AND WARMLY WELCOME YOU ALL TO THIS MEETING, IMPORTANT FOR TWO REASONS. THE FIRST REASON IS THE FINAL ESTABLISHMENT OF THE BANKING ASSOCIATION OF THE FEDERATION OF BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA. THE SECOND REASON, BUT NOT LESS IMPORTANT, AS IT DIRECTLY ARISES FROM THE FIRST ONE, IS FURTHER CONSOLIDATION AND INTEGRATION OF BANKING SECTOR. GLOBALISATION IS A MAJOR FEATURE OF THE PRESENT STAGE OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT WORLDWIDE. HOWEVER, THE FINANCIAL GLOBALISATION IS GROWING FAR MORE QUICKLY THAN REAL GLOBALISATION AND CONSOLIDATION. IN THAT RESPECT BIH IS NOT AN EXCEPTION. ON THE CONTRARY, IN BIH THE REFORM IN THE BANKING SECTOR, HAS GONE FURTHER AND FASTER THAN REFORM IN ANY OTHER SECTOR OF THE ECONOMY. IF WE LOOK BACK IT CAN BE SEEN THAT 6 YEARS AGO, WHEN THE CBBH COMMENCED ITS OPERATIONS, THERE WERE 76 ORGANISATIONS AUTHORISED TO BE BANKS IN BIH. BUT NONE OF THEM OPERATED OVER THE WHOLE THE COUNTRY AND MOST OF THEM WERE VERY SMALL. FRANKLY, IT WAS A RATHER STRANGE BANKING SYSTEM. TODAY, WE STILL HAVE SOME DISTANCE TO GO TO HAVE A EUROPEAN-TYPE BANKING SYSTEM, BUT EVERY DAY WE ARE GETTING CLOSER AND CLOSER TO IT. I BELIEVE THAT FOLLOWING TODAYS CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY OF THE FEDERATION BANKING ASSOCIATION AND SIGNING OF ITS STATUTE, THE ASSOCIATION WILL BECOME THE MAIN VOICE OF ALL BANKERS TOGETHER. I WOULD MUCH PREFER IT THAT YOU ESTABLISHED A SINGLE BANKING ASSOCIATION THAT REPRESENTED ALL BANKS IN BIH. BUT HAVING BANKING ASSOCIATIONS IN EACH ENTITY IS A STEP IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION. IN FUTURE, WHEN THE CBBH NEEDS TO MEET WITH COMMERCIAL BANKS IT WILL INVITE BOTH ENTITY BANKING ASSOCIATIONS TO PARTICIPATE. I HOPE THAT THE TWO ASSOCIATIONS WILL QUICKLY MOVE TO FORM SOME TYPE OF UMBRELLA ORGANISATION THAT WILL REPRESENT YOUR JOINT INTERESTS. YOUR ASSOCIATION WILL BE ABLE TO PERFORM SEVERAL IMPORTANT FUNCTIONS FOR YOU. IT WILL HELP PROTECT THE INTERESTS OF BANK MEMBERS AT THE INSTITUTIONAL AND GOVERNMENT BODIES, IT WILL PROMOTE THE BANKING SECTOR, IT CAN HELP DRAFT BANKING CODE WHICH HAS TO BE BASED ON PROFESSIONALISM AND HEALTHY COMPETITION THAT BENEFITS BOTH MEMBERS AND CONSUMERS, AS WELL AS TO PROMOTE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING OF BANKING SERVICES AND OVERALL FINANCIAL LITERACY. HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT IN BANKS IS CRUCIAL. THEREFORE, ONE OF THE IMPORTANT ACTIVITIES OF THE BANKING ASSOCIATION SHOULD ALSO BE STAFF TRAINING. PERHAPS THERE IS NO NEED FOR SETTING UP A FORMAL BANKING INSTITUTE, BUT CERTAINLY SOME FORM OF TRAINING PROGRAMME SHOULD EXIST UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE BANKING ASSOCIATION. ALTHOUGH BANKS ARE ALREADY GIVEN THE OPPORTUNITY TO COMMENT ON NEW BANKING LEGISLATION THE DEADLINES TEND TO BE TIGHT. SINCE THERE IS A GENERAL LACK OF OVERALL OVERSIGHT CONCERNING LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND AMENDMENTS IT IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT TO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO COMMMENT ON DRAFTS OF ALL LAWS WHICH HAVE AN IMPACT ON THE FINANCIAL SECTOR, NOT JUST BANKING BUT SECURITIES AND INSURANCE LAWS. IN THE PAST, WHEN THE CBBH NEEDED BANK REPRESENTATIVES IN ORGANISATIONS LIKE THE NATIONAL PAYMENTS COUNCIL WE SELECTED THE BANKERS OURSELVES. WE ALWAYS TRIED TO GET A GROUP THAT COVERED ALL REGIONS, ALL SIZES AND ALL TYPES OF OWNERSHIP. I AM NOT SURE IF WE ALWAYS SUCCEEDED. BUT IN FUTURE, WE WILL ASK THE ENTITY BANKING ASSOCIATIONS TO NOMINATE THE BANKING SECTOR REPRESENTATIVES ON SUCH GROUPS. THERE IS LOT OF CRITICISM TO BANKS FOR NOT LENDING ENOUGH AND UNDER MORE FAVOURABLE RATES AS WELL AS FOR HOLDING SO MUCH OF THEIR LIQUIDITY OUTSIDE BIH. WELL, SOME TIME AGO A CERTAIN BANKER WAS ASKED HOW COME THAT YOUR BANK OFFERS MUCH LOWER LENDING RATES IN AUSTRIA THAN IN BOSNIA AND WHEN WE WILL HAVE THE SAME RATES HERE? THE BANKER PROVIDED A VERY SIMPLE AND CORRECT ANSWER WHEN BOSNIA BECOMES LIKE AUSTRIA. BANKS ARE IN BUSINESS OF LENDING AS THAT IS HOW THEY EARN THEIR INCOME, BUT THEY WILL ONLY LEND IF THEY CAN BE CONFIDENT THAT THE CUSTOMER WILL PAY BACK THE LOAN OR IF HE DOES NOT THAT THEY CAN GO TO THE COURTS. LIKE MOST THINGS IN BIH THE COURT SYSTEM IS VERY COMPLEX AND IT TENDS TO MOVE VERY SLOWLY. FOR A COMMERCIAL SECTOR, INCLUDING THE BANKING SECTOR TO BE ABLE TO TAKE BUSINESS DECISIONS AND INVEST WITH CONFIDENCE IT MUST HAVE RECOURSE TO LEGAL REMEDIES AND COURTS TO RESOLVE DISPUTES QUICKLY AND FAIRLY. THE MACRO-ECONOMIC SITUATION IN BIH IS VERY STABLE. IT IS THE AREA OF REGULATORY, TAX AND LEGAL SYSTEM REFORM THAT WILL DETERMINE THE FUTURE OF BIH. THE CBBH WILL BE HAPPY TO WORK WITH YOUR ASSOCIATIONS TO PROMOTE THESE TYPES OF REFORMS.
